findings.title: Dead-code ApoClassLoader loads and instantiates classes from arbitrary file paths or URLs
findings.code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); ... c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); ... return c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: None in this variant. Constructor takes (path, classname); in applet mode (ApoConstants.B_APPLET == true, set by apoCommando/ApoMarioApplet.java:26) the path is used directly as a URL (line 68); otherwise as a local directory/jar path (line 66).
findings.sink: cl.loadClass(...).newInstance() at lines 73-75: arbitrary bytecode is defined, initialized, and its no-arg constructor executed.
findings.data_path: getMyClass() -> new URL(path) [applet] or new File(path).toURI().toURL() [desktop] -> URLClassLoader -> loadClass(classname) -> newInstance(). Verified unreachable: repo-wide grep for 'ApoClassLoader|getMyClass|Class.forName|newInstance' outside the definition returns zero hits; the only instantiations of game classes (ApoMarioMain.java:34-38, ApoMarioApplet.java:41-46) hardcode ApoMarioPanel.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical in this build: if a future edit or sibling-variant wiring calls new ApoClassLoader(url, 'evil.Evil').getMyClass(), any party controlling that URL (or a local user pointing it at a crafted directory) gets immediate constructor execution inside the game JVM. As shipped, no attacker-reachable path exists.
findings.preconditions: Some code must first be modified to invoke ApoClassLoader with an attacker-controlled path/classname (in sibling variants that use plugin-style loading this precondition may already hold - compare before scoring this variant).
findings.validation_plan: Compile the tree, then run a driver: new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8080/", "Evil").getMyClass(); with Evil.class (static block printing 'PWNED') served by python3 -m http.server 8080, after setting ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true. Observable result: 'PWNED' printed by the constructor proves the sink fires once a caller exists. Then confirm absence as shipped by showing javac -Xlint and a grep audit find no call sites.

findings.title: ApoIO level read/write uses plain HTTP (no TLS, no integrity check) in applet mode; machinery present but unwired
findings.code_excerpt: URL connectionURL = new URL(fileName); HttpURLConnection connection = (HttpURLConnection)connectionURL.openConnection(); connection.setDoOutput(true); data = new DataOutputStream(connection.getOutputStream());
findings.entry_point: readLevel(String)/writeLevel(String) (lines 31, 67). When B_APPLET==false fileName is a filesystem path (FileInputStream/FileOutputStream lines 36, 79); when true it is treated as a URL: writeLevel POSTs the level bytes to it (lines 40-43) and readLevel does connection.openStream() (lines 83-84).
findings.sink: Unauthenticated cleartext HTTP GET/POST to whatever host is embedded in fileName; response bytes flow into the abstract readLevel(DataInputStream) parser (line 87).
findings.data_path: Caller-supplied fileName string -> new URL(fileName) -> HttpURLConnection/openStream -> DataInputStream -> abstract parse. Verified unreachable in THIS variant: nothing extends ApoIO and grep for 'readLevel|writeLevel|DataInputStream|DataOutputStream' under apoCommando/ returns zero hits; levels come only from hardcoded ApoMarioMyLevels.LEVEL_STRINGS (apoCommando/level/ApoMarioMyLevels.java:8-11) matched in apoCommando/panels/ApoMarioModel.java:239-262 and apoCommando/level/ApoMarioLevel.java:207-253.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical here: were the applet wired like sibling variants (e.g., fetching get_level.php / posting save_highscore.php over http://), a MITM on the player's LAN could tamper with downloaded level bytes (parsed by hand with no schema check downstream) and forge submitted scores. As shipped, there is no call site, so no network traffic occurs at all.
findings.preconditions: Game running as signed applet (B_APPLET=true) AND a code change that subclasses ApoIO and passes an http:// fileName; additionally the abstract parser would need to tolerate attacker-chosen byte streams.
findings.validation_plan: (1) Prove the sink works: write a test subclass implementing readLevel(DataOutputStream)/readLevel(DataInputStream), run against a local netcat listener: java -cp . Test write http://127.0.0.1:9999/lvl -> observe plaintext POST body in nc (confirms no TLS/no signing); serve bytes from nc and observe them reaching the parser. (2) Prove absence as shipped: grep -rn 'extends ApoIO' and 'readLevel(' across all 72 files returns only the definitions in ApoIO.java itself.

findings.title: MD5 helper (MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")) in shared ApoHelp, unused in this variant
findings.code_excerpt: MessageDigest lDigest = MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"); lDigest.update(pInput.getBytes()); BigInteger lHashInt = new BigInteger(1, lDigest.digest()); return String.format("%1$032X", lHashInt);
findings.entry_point: Static method ApoHelp.getMd5Digest(String pInput) (line 305). No entry point exists: grep across the whole variant finds the single definition and zero callers.
findings.sink: MD5 digest computation intended (per corpus pattern) for score/validation tokens; collision-prone and unkeyed, so any future integrity check built on it is forgeable by construction.
findings.data_path: In this build: none - dead code. In sibling variants that call it around highscore submission, the data path is typically playerName+score -> getMd5Digest -> token sent alongside the score over plain HTTP, trivially recomputed by an attacker.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical here: a local player who wants to cheat needs nothing this function provides (achievements live only in memory, see ApoMarioAchievements.java:46-65; no scores leave the machine). If a future edit adds score validation using this helper, both attacker-forgery (choose colliding input) and simple recompute-the-hash forgery apply.
findings.preconditions: Someone must first wire getMd5Digest into a validation/submission path (as some sibling variants reportedly do).
findings.validation_plan: (1) Show the weakness generically: call ApoHelp.getMd5Digest on two known MD5 colliding blocks (e.g., the Daum-Luty 128-byte pair) and print identical output. (2) Show non-use as shipped: compile with a stub that throws from getMd5Digest and run the game normally (java apoCommando.ApoMarioMain, play a level, type commands in the DOS console) - no exception, confirming the code never executes.

categories_checked_and_absent: unsafe_custom_parser - no save/replay/level files are parsed: levels are procedural (ApoMarioRandomLevel) or from the hardcoded LEVEL_STRINGS array (ApoMarioMyLevels.java:8-11); the DOS-console input is compared against string literals or parsed with bounded Integer.parseInt in try/catch (ApoMarioModel.java:266-286)

path_traversal - no user-controlled filenames reach File/FileInputStream/FileOutputStream; the only such sinks (ApoIO.java:36,79; ApoMidiPlayer.java:64; ApoCopy.java:53-58) are never invoked, and ApoMarioMain.main ignores args (ApoMarioMain.java:23-25)
credential_or_secret_exposure - no credentials, tokens, or keys in the tree

information_disclosure - nothing is transmitted at runtime; clipboard helpers (ApoHelp.java:320-345) are uncalled; images load only from the classpath (all ApoMarioImageContainer.java:47-68 calls pass bLoad=false)

resource_exhaustion - level dimensions derive from constants/random bounded values (width 100-600 tiles, ApoMarioLevel.java:259); 'dif x' command clamped to 1..4 (ApoMarioModel.java:271-278); no loops sized by external input
client_side_trust - there is no server-side state to cheat: no highscores, no purchases, no remote accounts; achievements are in-memory ArrayLists lost on exit (ApoMarioAchievements.java:59-65)
notes: Effective project root is corpus/java/ApoCommando/Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoCommando (the corpus folder wraps an absolute-path copy); all cited paths are relative to that root. Identity note: despite ApoMario*-class prefixes, this IS ApoCommando - the in-game console prints 'ApoCommando (version ...)' (ApoMarioModel.java:109) and there is an 'apocommando' easter egg (ApoMarioModel.java:388); the separate corpus entry ApoMario is almost certainly a later rename/descendant, so flaws in the shared org/apogames layer likely propagate between them. Method: all 72 files were swept with pattern searches covering network APIs, serialization, digests, classloading, native loading, file IO, exec/env, clipboard, and sound/image loading; ~20 files were read in depth, including every file with any hit and all entry points. Bottom line: the runtime-wired attack surface is keyboard/mouse only; there is no persistence, no socket, no deserialization, and no secret. All three real weaknesses (class loader, plain-HTTP IO, MD5) are cloned library infrastructure that this variant inherits but never invokes - exactly the clone-and-own latency risk this audit is meant to measure: harmless here today, one-line activation away tomorrow.
